correctness.rationale: Each output word maps to a unique path-prefix counting vector in a four-state de Bruijn graph. Saturation at two preserves exactly the zero/one/multiple distinction, so the deterministic language accepts precisely singleton-predecessor outputs. The complete reachable saturated graph has thirty states and four accepting states. From that graph an exact integer whole-vector identity (T^9-T^8-T^7+T^6-2T^4-T^3-T-I)f=-2e0 and the fact Te0=0 imply the all-length recurrence. Ten directly evaluated coefficients fix the rational generating function. The standalone verify.py was executed from its actual final package path; its exact graph, identity and generating series checks passed, as did independent direct enumeration for output lengths 1 through 13. No infinite claim relies on those finite examples alone.

value.rationale: A finite output with one predecessor is an intrinsically motivated exact reconstruction event, not an arbitrary slice of a table. The theorem gives the full all-length singleton population of the well-studied nonlinear binary majority local rule, including a degree-nine rational series and recurrence and a concise reproducible thirty-state mechanism. Attainable-output counts in earlier image studies do not answer this more discriminating invertibility question; the exact spectrum makes a natural addition to finite preimage and zero-error sensor reconstruction theory. It is not asserted to be a new general preimage-count algorithm.
